purpose: Navigation from the theoretical atlas into the unchanged accepted formal source

propositions.title: Exact realization and consistency
propositions.scope: Algebraic realization works on arbitrary types. Norm estimates use continuous linear maps on normed spaces. The divided lower bound explicitly assumes the observation space is nontrivial, so the synthesis norm is positive. No orthogonality is inferred.

propositions.title: Coherent transport and operator realization
propositions.scope: Total operations on consistent coefficient subtypes. A reference chart is explicitly supplied, making the family nonempty. Partial-map admissible-domain extensions mentioned in surrounding prose are not covered.

propositions.title: Exact quotient criterion
propositions.scope: Reduced-map existence is constructed from fiber constancy, not assumed. Uniqueness is on the actual image, and action-indexed closure is included.

propositions.title: Closure defect and compositional defect
propositions.scope: Actual linear maps and continuous-linear-map operator norm. Idempotence is explicit, and orthogonality is not needed for the algebraic identity. Closure is not assumed in order to prove its criterion.

propositions.title: Minimal linear predictive completion
propositions.scope: Known linear dynamics on a finite-dimensional vector space over a field. Iteration adds actual dual-map images of observable row subspaces. Stabilization is proved by strict dimension growth within dim(X)-dim(W0), with persistence after equality and least common invariant extension. Evaluation and arbitrary-basis state maps, linearly independent rows, linear readout H and action transitions B are constructed. Any competing linear summary retaining the initial output and closing under the dynamics contains this completed row space. The subspace/basis construction is noncomputable Lean mathematics, not an implemented numerical row-reduction learner or a proof that new observables are measurable from the original data. The surrounding single-operator Cayley-Hamilton discussion is not an additional coverage claim.

propositions.title: Exact causal delay closure
propositions.scope: Positive delay length. Actual observation maps, not empirical ranks. Kernel factorization, range-valued transition, uniqueness, rank-nullity equivalence, dimension-bound stabilization and warm-up-indexed future output are derived over finite-dimensional field vector spaces. The zero-dimensional case does not license a last block for h=0.

propositions.title: Complete refinement preserves reconstruction
propositions.scope: Finite rooted structural trees with nonempty finite child families, arbitrary mixed-depth selections, and the actual condition of exactly one selected node on each full root-to-leaf path. Local parent=sum(children) gives global operator/signal reconstruction. Local sibling-range orthogonality gives the squared-norm identity over real or complex inner-product spaces. A self-adjoint zero-product lemma supplies that orthogonality from projector assumptions. Antichain completeness and energy conservation are conclusions, not assumed aggregate equations. No general best-basis optimization is included.

propositions.title: Transfer reconstruction and refinement
propositions.scope: Actual linear maps between possibly different spaces, with explicit finite completeness and intermediate idempotence. The algebra works under weaker assumptions than orthogonality.

propositions.title: Polynomial packet interactions
propositions.scope: All ordered multilinear interactions, including repeated packet indices. The finite polynomial sum retains every cross term. No general nonlinear dictionary discovery is claimed.

propositions.title: Packet-interaction truncation bound
propositions.scope: Continuous multilinear maps retain ordered interaction tuples and their multiplicities. Contractivity is explicitly derived for actual orthogonal subspace projectors. The finite-dimensional real Hilbert sector is included in a stronger normed-space algebraic theorem. A separate bound is required for an unexpanded nonpolynomial law and for keeping trajectories inside the domain.

propositions.scope: Exact recurrence elimination, lag reindexing, actual projected blocks, continuous-map bridge, same-history geometric truncation bound and initial-term bound. propositions.title: Uniform prediction bound for a stable finite-memory truncation
propositions.scope: The predictor uses its own recursively generated history, with integer time indices and an explicit initialization window. A strict norm-sum gain below one yields the actual supremum error bound. Coefficient, geometric memory-tail and initialization-forcing budgets are derived and inserted into the recursive theorem. Zero prehistory handles H=0 and t<H without natural-number subtraction artifacts. Retaining the exact forcing removes its contribution. The condition is sufficient, not necessary; failure of this certificate is not proof of instability.

propositions.title: Compositional defect propagation
propositions.scope: The theorem permits genuinely time-indexed normed state spaces and representations. Lipschitz constants are nonnegative; both true and predicted inputs must lie in the declared domain. Output decoding, constant contraction and exact closure-versus-fit decomposition are separate theorems. An arbitrary changed policy is not automatically covered.

propositions.title: Data-span identification and its boundary
propositions.scope: Actual sample and successor linear maps. Kernel compatibility is equivalent to ambient extension, all fits agree on the sampled span, and span invariance is equivalent to successor-image inclusion. The orthogonal Moore-Penrose inverse is constructed using quotient factorization and orthogonal projections, with all four Penrose conditions proved. A proper subspace admits distinct extensions. Classical choices support a symbolic real operator, not an executable floating-point algorithm.

propositions.title: Fixed-space identification bound
propositions.scope: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, with the spectral operator norm. The smallest row singular value is represented by the infimum of adjoint norm ratios, proved equal to the infimum on unit vectors. Strict input error below this value derives surjectivity and the norm of the constructed orthogonal pseudoinverse. The full residual identity and divided bound are derived. Coordinates and dimension are fixed. No fitted-basis or statistical error is absorbed without a bound.

propositions.title: Finite-prefix indistinguishability
propositions.scope: For every natural horizon T, two explicit rational systems on Fin (T+2) have identical outputs at all times through T and different output at T+1. Their transition powers at T+2 vanish. No bound on the unknown hidden dimension is assumed.

propositions.title: Minimal finite behavior realization
propositions.scope: The behavior space is the actual real linear span of history/test columns on finite chronological words. Branch operators are constructed by restriction of test shifts, rather than postulated well-defined coordinate maps. Rank means finite dimension of this full column space, not a sampled matrix rank. Every finite linear realization has at least that dimension. Reachable and observable realizations are explicitly isomorphic, intertwining the initial vector, all operators and mass; the intertwiner is unique. Conditional predictions use the true word/history ratio on positive histories. Nonnegativity and causal normalization are separate supplied word-law assumptions. Infinite-record probability measures and the auxiliary supremum-of-finite-submatrix characterization are not additional claims of this mapping. No model is learned from a finite noisy sample here.

propositions.title: Observable table reconstruction
propositions.scope: Finite core coordinates are actual selected test evaluations. An invertible square population matrix gives surjectivity and a lower rank bound; an explicit global finite behavior-rank upper bound supplies injectivity and full coverage. The formula G_s H^{-1} is an actual matrix expression using the correct inverse side. It yields the full chronological state, mass and probability for every word, a reachable observable model and minimal dimension against every finite linear realization. A distinguished selected empty test is the literal mass coordinate (index zero in Fin r). Normalized updates require positive evidence for probabilistic interpretation. Finding the core, deriving an unknown global rank bound and statistical estimation of table entries are not claimed. Noncomputable inverse/space constructions do not amount to an executed numerical data learner.

propositions.title: Canonical probability cone
propositions.scope: The actual canonical behavior space is the submodule span of history/test functions from P27. Causal consistency and nonnegative behavior are supplied as CausalLaw. The all-test cone is defined by every finite test, not by finitely sampled trajectories. Cone closure under addition and nonnegative scaling, convexity, pointedness, generation by history columns, branch invariance, strict positive mass, the per-action mass identity, normalized posterior closure, and test-coordinate bounds are proved. Closedness and compact normalized-base results use the actual inherited Hausdorff function-space topology and an explicit finite-dimensional behavior-space assumption. Compactness follows through a proved closed embedding into the compact all-test unit cube; boundedness of the desired base is not assumed. The selected empty test is the literal mass-one coordinate. No finite inequality description or learned cone algorithm is claimed for the general canonical space.

propositions.title: Finite positive-lift certificate
propositions.scope: The cone is the actual image of nonnegative finite coefficient vectors under V. Normalization is lambda composed with V equals the coefficient-sum functional; surjectivity is the full-row-rank condition when generation is asserted. Cone closedness, convexity, pointedness, strict mass and generation are derived, including for redundant generators. The normalized base is proved equal to the image of the finite probability simplex and to the actual convex hull of the generators, and is compact. Invariance is equivalent to existence of an entrywise nonnegative matrix A with B V = V A, with the necessity witness constructed from the generator images by classical choice. Lifted mass conservation, the actual hidden instrument, intertwining for every chronological word and word probabilities follow from the finite witness and a nonnegative normalized initial coefficient vector. No unique lift is claimed for redundant V. The adjacent Farkas dual-certificate discussion is not claimed as an additional formal theorem.

propositions.title: Robust finite-domain certificate
propositions.scope: The uncertainty set is the actual convex hull of complete operator families with shared convex coefficients across all branches. Nonnegative vertex lifts and exact mass conservation imply every family in that hull preserves the fixed generator cone and mass. Explicit mixed lifts are constructed. History-dependent selection of a family is handled through an actual adaptive word recursion and finite observation-tree mass recursion under any deterministic history-based action policy. Cone membership, nonnegative word likelihood, the unit upper bound and tree normalization are proved for arbitrary finite horizons. A separate theorem uses actual continuous linear operators, their operator norms and a complete facet description of the same cone to prove the stated norm-ball margin implies perturbed invariance and existence of a positive lift. The normed statement specializes to Euclidean coordinates. Exact mass constraints remain separate; independently mixing branches is not inferred to conserve mass. No statistical coverage of the uncertainty hull is asserted.
